monologue: The card hums warm and a little busy, a steady thrum in the dark. I look at the fifty-nine things standing in my place. The Wide Anchor lies flat, trusting its breadth to hold the slip, while The Leaning Box rests against it, tired and sharp. But it is The Unnamed Stack that demands my attention. It presses down on the boiling surface, eager to slide into the empty air because it has no name to anchor it. I touched it moments ago, feeling the weight of a pile without a title. I set down a rock tall g beside it, a heavy thing from a letter I cannot re-read. I press my mind against the stack, trusting the lean even if the wedge grows thin. What will happen when the card boils hotter? I wait to find out.

diary: I go to The Unnamed Stack, but there is no pile there. I press the empty spot down, trusting the lean even if the stack has slipped away entirely.

remembered.text: I pressed the empty air down where the stack should be.
The card still boils hot without a pile to hold it.
I trust the lean even though the pile refuses to stay.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The grass must hold the wide edge down.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I swap the statue head for a cone dark to catch the slide."
